predecessors.name: Warring States Japan
predecessors.text: Satsuma, Ōsumi and the southern half of Hyūga

successors.name: Satsuma Domain
successors.text: Satsuma, Ōsumi and the southern half of Hyūga

ledger.x: 1576: the first dated event on the pages.
10 December 1578: Mimigawa on the Mimi River in Hyūga, a Shimazu victory; Toshihisa pursued survivors to the Ōtomo headquarters at Matsuyama castle.
1581: 'His forces took Minamata castle in Higo Province with 115,000 men'; the Aso clan was defeated in early 1584.
3 May 1584: Okitanawate near Shimabara in Hizen, the combined Shimazu and Arima forces against the Ryūzōji; Ryūzōji Takanobu killed, 10,000 Ryūzōji dead.
1585: Horikiri Castle in Chikugo attacked and Iwaya Castle taken after the invasion of Chikuzen; by mid-1585 the Shimazu controlled both.
1586: the Shimazu 'seized Funai Castle from the Ōtomo'; 'Bungo province fell to them' after Hetsugigawa.
1587: Hidenaga landed south of Bungo and attacked the Shimazu at Takajō in Hyūga; the infobox gives 1586-1587 for the campaign.
June 1587; the Kyūshū campaign page: the Shimazu surrendered later in 1587, Kagoshima not attacked.

1587 settlement: the Shimazu 'kept Satsuma and Ōsumi Province, plus half of Hyūga'; 'most conquered domains went to Katō, Konishi, and Kuroda', northern Kyushu fiefs to the Mōri, Chikuzen to Kobayakawa.
1600-1601: 'Shimazu Iehisa was created the first Lord of Satsuma' in 1601; the Satsuma Domain page dates the domain from 1600.

wars.name: Shimazu–Ōtomo war in Hyūga
wars.outcome: The Shimazu won at Takabaru (1576) and Mimigawa (10 December 1578); the Ōtomo lost several commanders.

wars.name: Shimazu campaigns in Higo and Hizen
wars.outcome: Minamata in Higo (1581); Okitanawate in Hizen (3 May 1584), Ryūzōji Takanobu killed; the Aso defeated.

wars.name: Shimazu invasion of Chikugo, Chikuzen and Bungo
wars.outcome: Horikiri and Iwaya in 1585; Tachibana and Funai in 1586; Bungo fell after Hetsugigawa.

wars.name: Kyūshū campaign
wars.outcome: The Shimazu were driven back from Hyūga and routed in Satsuma; they sued for peace in June 1587 and kept Satsuma, Ōsumi and half of Hyūga.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, battles and provinces, not borders; the provinces are drawn as prefectures and the Kyushu frontiers moved each year.
